answer: Each identity is a signal etched into the basalt, a single append-only registry. Etching another signal requires burning pigment, priced by the basalt at everything burned this epoch: the tenth signal costs ten units, the thousandth costs a thousand. The counter lives in the basalt and updates atomically, so clones cannot split the bill — k clones cost k squared. Break: a fork that resets the pigment counter cheapens clones again, so the basalt must stay single and final.
